MS

Mass spectrometry characterization

Confirm what you made: intact mass, sequence coverage, post-translational modifications, glycans and process impurities.

Assays
4
Standard turnaround
3–12 days
Fastest priority slot
2 days

Most programs come to us with one question: is this molecule what we think it is? Our mass spectrometry group answers it at three levels, from intact and subunit mass down to residue-level modifications, so you can see clipping, oxidation, deamidation or a missing glycan before it shows up as a surprise in stability data.

Every study starts from your sequence file. We build the search database with you, agree the modifications to look for, and report coverage against the full sequence rather than a percentage alone.

Questions this answers

  • Is the expressed protein the right sequence and mass?
  • Which residues are oxidized or deamidated after stress?
  • How does the glycan profile shift between clones or runs?
  • Which host cell proteins persist after purification?

Sample requirements

Sample requirements for mass spectrometry characterization
Minimum amount50 µg per sample (10 µg for peptides)
Concentration0.5 mg/mL or higher
BufferAvoid PEG, glycerol above 5% and non-volatile detergents
ShippingFrozen on dry ice, or 2–8 °C if shipped same day

What you receive

  • Deconvoluted spectra with annotated mass assignments
  • Sequence coverage map and modification table
  • Raw data files in vendor and open formats
  • Methods section written for your report or filing
